intro: IGES to STL converts IGES files to STL, the format every slicer reads, on the server with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print an IGES model from a supplier or an old archive.
IGES is the oldest CAD exchange format, still common in moulds, tooling and supplier files, with exact surfaces and solids. Here it is converted to STL.

The conversion is done by OpenCascade: it reads each part with its name and colour (also each face's), turns the file's units into millimetres and tessellates its surfaces into triangles. Choose the STL quality: low for light files, medium for most parts and high so the IGES's holes and curves come out smooth.

Each file is converted in an isolated process with bounded memory and time on our server in the European Union, up to five files per task, and deleted when it expires. You can keep the IGES parts separate in the STL, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

To print an IGES model from a supplier or an old archive, it is worth checking the STL before using it: open it in your viewer or slicer, check that the parts and their measurements match the IGES and, if something comes out sideways or too faceted, convert it again with other options. The result note summarises the parts, the triangles and what was done with the IGES.
steps: Upload one or more IGES files.
Choose the quality and, optionally, the units, scale and parts.

faq.q: Which quality should I choose for the IGES?
faq.a: Medium works for almost everything; high for small parts with holes and curves, and low if the STL made from the IGES is too heavy.
The colours of the IGES parts and faces go into the STL if it is 3MF, OBJ or GLB; STL stores no colours.

faq.q: What happens to the IGES measurements?
faq.a: OpenCascade turns the IGES measurements into millimetres in the STL, which is what slicers and CAD programs expect.
